universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.notes: DPOR's ULR page: 'Universal License Recognition makes it easy for qualified out-of-state applicants already holding a valid license or certification in another state to get licensed in Virginia', for applicants licensed or certified in that state 'for at least one year'; its list of ULR applications includes 'Contractors - Tradesman' (electricians are tradesmen). Separate from the bilateral agreements in reciprocityRules.

compactMembership.notes: Virginia's electrician reciprocity operates via named bilateral agreements and ULR — neither is a single multistate compact license practiced across member states without a new license (the defining feature of a true compact). Recorded as false to avoid conflating these real mechanisms with a compact under this field's actual schema meaning.

reciprocityRules.value: DPOR's list of Board for Contractors reciprocal licensing/examination agreements names three for Journeyman Electrical Tradesman: District of Columbia (Journeyman and Master Electrical Tradesman, license and examination reciprocity), Kentucky (Electrician and Master Electrician, examination reciprocity) and West Virginia (Journeyman and Master Electrical Tradesman, examination reciprocity). Maryland's agreement is Master-only and does not cover Journeyman. Virginia's Universal License Recognition is a separate pathway; see universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.
reciprocityRules.sourceName: Virginia Department of Professional and Occupational Regulation (DPOR), Board for Contractors

history.newValue: Virginia has real, named bilateral reciprocal examination agreements for the Journeyman Electrician license with exactly two states: Kentucky (Journeyman Electrician <-> VA Journeyman) and West Virginia (Journeyman <-> VA Journeyman). Maryland's agreement is Master-only and does NOT cover Journeyman — a Maryland Journeyman certificate does not qualify under this reciprocal agreement. A separate Universal License Recognition (ULR) pathway may independently apply to applicants from other states — see universalLicenseRecognitionStatus.
